title.en: Written tanween changes and mixed decision practice

source.book: Tajweed Rules of the Qur'an — Part One
source.verification: book section reviewed; examples reused from verified lessons

prerequisites: Recognize noon saakinah and all tanween forms.
Know the trigger groups for izhar, idgham, iqlab, and ikhfa'.
Apply each rule in guided recitation.
learningOutcomes: Use Mushaf clues such as the small mim without relying on them alone.
Apply one decision routine to all four rules.
Classify mixed noon-saakinah and tanween boundaries.
Explain every answer by naming the target and immediate next letter.
Recite a mixed set with teacher-approved rule application.

linguistic.ar: المراجعة هي إعادة النظر لتثبيت العلم وتصحيح الخطأ.
linguistic.en: Review means revisiting knowledge to strengthen it and correct errors.

technical.ar: المراجعة الشاملة تجمع أحكام النون الساكنة والتنوين الأربعة في تطبيق واحد: الإظهار، والإدغام، والإقلاب، والإخفاء، مع الاستفادة من علامات المصحف والتحقق دائمًا من الحرف التالي.
technical.en: This cumulative review combines izhar, idgham, iqlab, and ikhfa' in one decision process, using Mushaf clues while always verifying the immediately following letter.

studentFriendly.ar: لا تخمّن الحكم من شكل الكلمة. حدّد النون الساكنة أو التنوين، ثم انظر إلى الحرف التالي مباشرة وضعه في مجموعته.
studentFriendly.en: Do not guess from the word shape. Find noon saakinah or tanween, inspect the next letter, and place it in its rule group.

definition.memoryFormula: الهدف ← الحرف التالي ← مجموعة الحرف ← الحكم ← طريقة النطق

keyTerms.en: a written recitation clue in the Mushaf
the small mim clue for iqlab

teacherPreparation: Mix examples rather than presenting them rule by rule.
Hide rule colors during the mastery check.
Use the same decision sentence for every answer.

openingReview.teacherPrompt: Ask the learner to name all four rules.
Rebuild the trigger map from memory.
Ask what the small mim sign indicates.

conceptExplanation.text: Mushaf signs can help, but the reliable method is always to locate the target and inspect the immediate next letter.
Use this lesson as both instruction and assessment. Record recognition and recitation mastery separately.

lessonPath.title: Inspect
lessonPath.text: Read only the immediate next letter.

lessonPath.title: Group
lessonPath.text: Place the trigger in one of four groups.

lessonPath.title: Perform
lessonPath.text: Apply clarity, merging, change, or concealment.

lessonPath.title: Verify
lessonPath.text: Use teacher listening and Mushaf clues.

visualExplanation.display: ء ه ع ح غ خ = إظهار | ي ن م و ل ر = إدغام | ب = إقلاب | الباقي 15 = إخفاء
visualExplanation.teacherUse: Cover the map during independent classification.

ruleSummary.condition: Noon saakinah or tanween is followed by another letter.
ruleSummary.result: The immediate next letter selects izhar, idgham, iqlab, or ikhfa'.
ruleSummary.location: Within one word or across two words according to each rule and its exceptions.

quranExamples.readingInstruction: Merge into ya with two-count ghunnah.
Merge directly into ra without a two-count ghunnah.
quranExamples.teacherExplanation: Ra belongs to the ل ر group.

quranExamples.readingInstruction: Change to hidden mim with two-count ghunnah.
quranExamples.teacherExplanation: Ba is the single iqlab trigger.
Shin is one of the fifteen ikhfa' letters.
quranExamples.commonError: Making noon fully clear or fully merged.

quranExamples.readingInstruction: Change tanween to hidden mim before ba.
quranExamples.teacherExplanation: The small mim is a visual clue, confirmed by ba.
quranExamples.commonError: Using the sign without checking the trigger.

guidedPractice.teacherAction: Display a mixed boundary with colors hidden.
guidedPractice.studentAction: State target, next letter, group, rule, and performance.
guidedPractice.feedback: Return to the first incorrect decision step.

guidedPractice.teacherAction: Reveal the Mushaf clue after the learner decides.
guidedPractice.studentAction: Use it to verify rather than replace reasoning.
guidedPractice.feedback: Separate identification score from recitation score.

interactiveActivities.feedbackCorrect: Correct. Confirm it by finding ba.
interactiveActivities.feedbackIncorrect: The small mim points to changed mim quality.

interactiveActivities.feedbackIncorrect: Start with the target and immediate next letter.

instruction.en: A learner checks a later ba instead of the immediate qaf.

interactiveActivities.feedbackCorrect: Correct. Only the immediate next letter matters.
interactiveActivities.feedbackIncorrect: Do not skip qaf to reach ba.

instruction.en: A learner sees a clue but cannot explain the trigger.

interactiveActivities.feedbackCorrect: Correct. The clue supports reasoning, not replaces it.

interactiveActivities.prompt: What order should always be used?
items: Target → next letter → group → rule → performance
acceptedAnswers: Target → next letter → group → rule → performance
interactiveActivities.feedbackCorrect: Excellent. This routine transfers to every mixed example.
interactiveActivities.feedbackIncorrect: Begin with the target and finish with performance.

interactiveActivities.feedbackCorrect: Correct. Recitation mastery is assessed separately by the teacher.
interactiveActivities.feedbackIncorrect: Knowledge and recitation have separate mastery checks.

commonMistakes: Guessing from a visual clue without checking the next letter.
Looking at a later letter instead of the immediate next letter.
Knowing the rule name but performing the wrong sound.
Treating recognition mastery as recitation mastery.
correctionTechniques: Return to the first incorrect decision step.
Keep a four-column map available, then gradually hide it.
Use previously mastered examples before unseen mixed examples.

knowledgeChecks.success: At least eight are correct with reasons.
Teacher approves rule application in two attempts.

teacherQuestions: How must the sound be performed?
studentTasks: Recite a balanced set from all four rules.
independentPractice: Classify ten teacher-approved boundaries before reciting.
homework: Prepare eight mixed examples: two from each main rule.
For every example write target, trigger, rule, and performance.
masteryCriteria: Uses the decision routine without prompting.
Classifies at least 8 of 10 mixed examples with reasons.
Performs all four rule outcomes accurately.
Passes teacher-observed recitation in two consecutive attempts.
teacherNotes: This lesson completes the unit but should also serve as a recurring spiral review.
Do not mark the unit mastered from quiz performance alone.
Keep a record of which trigger groups still cause hesitation.
Return to the relevant focused lesson when a repeated error appears.
sourceNotes: Examples are reused from source-verified lessons.
Mixed assessment and decision sequence are curriculum-design additions.
verificationStatus: unit synthesis complete; live teacher recitation assessment required
